*"Organic chemistry and beyond"*

::: {.callout-note}
## Key Revelation
Carbon's ability to form four bonds creates unlimited molecular possibilities. Add nitrogen, oxygen, and other atoms, and you have the chemistry of life.
:::

## Carbon: The Backbone of Complexity

Why carbon?
- 4 valence electrons → 4 bonds
- Can bond to itself → chains and rings
- Right size → stable bonds
- Multiple bond types → single, double, triple

## Hydrocarbons

Molecules of just carbon and hydrogen.

### Alkanes (Single Bonds)

| Formula | Name | Structure | Notes |
|---------|------|-----------|-------|
| CH₄ | Methane | Tetrahedral | Natural gas |
| C₂H₆ | Ethane | Two tetrahedra | |
| C₃H₈ | Propane | Chain | Fuel |
| C₄H₁₀ | Butane | Chain | Lighter fluid |
| C₅H₁₂ | Pentane | Chain | Solvent |

General formula: CₙH₂ₙ₊₂

### Alkenes (Double Bonds)

| Formula | Name | Notes |
|---------|------|-------|
| C₂H₄ | Ethylene | Planar, ripening agent |
| C₃H₆ | Propene | Plastic precursor |

General formula: CₙH₂ₙ

### Alkynes (Triple Bonds)

| Formula | Name | Notes |
|---------|------|-------|
| C₂H₂ | Acetylene | Linear, welding fuel |
| C₃H₄ | Propyne | |

General formula: CₙH₂ₙ₋₂

### Aromatic Compounds

Ring structures with alternating double bonds.

![Benzene ring structure: six carbons in a hexagonal ring with alternating double bonds.](../../media/images/fig-benzene.png){#fig-benzene}

Benzene (C₆H₆) features a six-membered ring with resonance: electrons delocalize around the entire ring rather than alternating between fixed single and double bonds.

## Functional Groups

The reactive parts of molecules.

| Group | Formula | Name | Example |
|-------|---------|------|---------|
| -OH | R-OH | Alcohol | Ethanol |
| -CHO | R-CHO | Aldehyde | Formaldehyde |
| -COOH | R-COOH | Carboxylic acid | Acetic acid |
| -NH₂ | R-NH₂ | Amine | Methylamine |
| -SH | R-SH | Thiol | Methanethiol |
| C=O | R-CO-R' | Ketone | Acetone |
| -O- | R-O-R' | Ether | Diethyl ether |
| -COO- | R-COO-R' | Ester | Ethyl acetate |

### Alcohols

Hydroxyl group (-OH) on carbon:

![Ethanol molecule showing hydroxyl group.](../../media/images/fig-ethanol.png){#fig-ethanol}

Ethanol (CH₃CH₂OH) is the "drinking alcohol" found in beer, wine, and spirits.

### Acids and Bases

**Carboxylic acids** donate H⁺: R-COOH → R-COO⁻ + H⁺

**Amines** accept H⁺: R-NH₂ + H⁺ → R-NH₃⁺

## Isomers

Same formula, different structure.

### Structural Isomers

Different connectivity: **Butane** (CH₃-CH₂-CH₂-CH₃) is a straight chain, while **Isobutane** (CH₃-CH(CH₃)-CH₃) is branched. Same formula (C₄H₁₀), different structure.

### Stereoisomers

Same connectivity, different spatial arrangement:
- **Cis-trans**: Around double bonds
- **Enantiomers**: Mirror images (chirality)

### Chirality

A carbon with 4 different groups is chiral:

![Chirality: a carbon bonded to four different groups has non-superimposable mirror images.](../../media/images/fig-chirality.png){#fig-chirality}

Mirror images are not superimposable. This matters in biology: life uses only one "handedness" of amino acids.

## Reactions

### Combustion

CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O + energy

### Substitution
One group replaces another.

### Addition
Atoms add across double bond.

### Elimination
Double bond forms, atoms leave.

## Concepts

- **hydrocarbon**: C and H only
- **functional-group**: Reactive part of molecule
- **isomer**: Same formula, different structure
- **chirality**: Mirror-image asymmetry
